evidence: Ov. M. 1.105: in dūrīs haerentia mōra rubētīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a mulberry; a blackberry”. Ovid’s are the ones that cling to the brambles.
The berry named in full, as the herbalist Mattioli does. Mōrum alone is enough wherever a mulberry cannot be meant.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
